label: TP
reason: Both alerts are True Positives. Alert 1 (XSS): User input ('param') flows through an ArrayList rotation (adding/removing elements) to become 'bar', which is concatenated into 'fileName'. 'fileName' is printed to the response writer without HTML encoding, reflecting user input into the HTML body. Alert 2 (Path Injection): The same flow leads to 'fileName' being passed to 'new File()', creating a file path dependent entirely on user input without validation. Neither sink is sanitized.

evidence.note: User input 'param' extracted from request and rotated into 'bar' via ArrayList manipulation (removes 'safe', keeps 'param')
Tainted 'bar' assigned to 'fileName' and printed to response without encodeForHTML (XSS sink); 'fileName' also passed to new File() (Path Injection sink)
